messages.subject: Re: Getting error using rep_len in simple script
messages.subject_clean: Getting error using rep_len in simple script
messages.body_plain:
Jeff,

you are right: the rep_len function was introduced in 3.0.0: "There is a new function rep_len() analogous to rep.int <http://rep.int>() for when speed is required (and names are not)." (source: http://cran.xl-mirror.nl/src/base/NEWS.html)

Renjin is forked from GNU R version 2.14.2 so this function is not available in Renjin and you should use the rep.int <http://rep.int> function instead. Renjin will probably be synced with later versions of R at some point in time (it's been done in the past), but at the moment we are focusing on increasing general compatibility.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan Kallen

I'm very new to R and Renjin.  I have some data in the form of  ArrayLists that I'd like to manipulate in R.  I seem to be able to access and assign the array successfully, but if I try to manipulate it I get an EvalException:

import(MyData);
import(java.util.ArrayList);

data <- MyData$new();
array <- c(data$getMyArrayList());

messages.subject: Re: How do I convert Lists into R vectors?
messages.subject_clean: How do I convert Lists into R vectors?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ron,
Right now, Renjin doesn't implicitly convert java collection objects to R objects -- so your "array" looks like an "external ptr" to the min() function, which is expecting a vector.

Renjin will however implicitly convert arrays of double[] to R objects that can be passed to R functions, so you might try array.toArray(Arrays.newArray...etc)

Implicit conversion from java.util collection objects on calls to functions might be very nice though, so open an issue on github if you think it's something worth having.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: GPLv3 => ASL, MIT, Mozilla, BSD license?
messages.subject_clean: GPLv3 => ASL, MIT, Mozilla, BSD license?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Otis,

Though I would love to license Renjin more liberally, we depend signficantly on the GPL-Licensed R-language base, stats, etc libraries from GNU R, so Renjin is even in the most creative of interpretations a derivative work of GNU R which confers certain obligations under the GPL.

However, we're committed to doing what ever we can to making it available in the widest range of use cases, for example, perhaps relicensing parts of it under LGPL, which I think would be consistent with the spirit of the GNU R licensing.

Can you tell me more about your use case and what problems that GPL would pose for you?

Best,

Alex
